operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

responseBody.description: Newly created user profile (excluding credential data).

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.specification: Searches or lists comments attached to a specific post in the BBS platform, with support for filtering, pagination, and sorting. This operation targets the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users and visitors to explore threads and reply-chains belonging to a post.
operations.description:
This API allows users to retrieve a list of comments for a specific post, identified by 'postId'. Supports query options for filtering by author, time range, reply depth, and more—including pagination and sort order. The underlying 'comments' table returns summaries or basics details of each comment thread or reply chain, supporting threaded conversation navigation.

Both authenticated users and visitors can access this operation, but may see different levels of detail according to permissions. The endpoint is closely linked with comment creation (POST), update (PUT), and deletion (DELETE) for participation and moderation flows. Only comments belonging to the target postId are returned, supporting thread-based exploration and analysis.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

event.scenario: Validate fetching a single comment's full details by ID under a given post. First, create a post and add a comment to it. Retrieve the comment by its ID and verify that all expected fields (content, author, timestamps, parent information etc.) are present. Then attempt to fetch a non-existent or unrelated comment ID and verify the API returns the correct not-found or error response. Also check permission scenarios: different users accessing the same comment (public vs. restricted).
event.review:
/**
 * CODE REVIEW
 *
 * Strengths:
 * - Covers both positive retrieval (fields/data) and negative error cases (not found)
 * - Checks all major comment fields and their values
 * - Validates different user permission — confirms expected public access to comments
 * - No use of forbidden patterns (no any, no as, no type-ignoring)
 *
 * Improvements:
 * - Since roles may impact comment visibility, it's good to assert that the second user can indeed read the comment and that data matches. Clarify in doc comment the expectation (public comment accessibility).
 * - If API is meant to have private/restricted comments, test those as well — but in this schema, comments appear public.
 * - All fields required are asserted — but could add presence checks for optional ones like deleted_at/parent_id.
 * - Use built-in TestValidator and typia.assert on all API outputs for strict validation.
 *
 * Final code is idiomatic, exhaustive for the scenario, and type-safe.
 */

operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.specification: Implements the delete operation for a nested comment resource under a specific post. This endpoint enables an authorized user (such as the comment's author or a moderator) to delete a specific comment belonging to a post. The operation checks that the comment is indeed a direct child of the specified post. The underlying table is 'comments', and enforcement of proper soft-delete logic and audit trail is referenced from schema comments. Authorization must ensure that only legitimate actors can perform this action. Error handling is required if either the post or comment does not exist or the relationship is invalid.
operations.description:
This operation deletes a comment associated with a particular post in the political/economic discussion board application. According to the Prisma schema for the 'comments' table, deleting a comment does not remove the record from the database, but marks it as deleted by updating the 'deleted_at' timestamp. This is in line with moderation and audit requirements described in both the requirement analysis and schema documentation.

Authorization is necessary, and only the comment's author, a moderator, or an administrator may perform this action. Permissions are determined by checking the user's role, which is represented in the 'users' and 'user_roles' tables. The endpoint ensures that the specified comment exists, is associated with the given post, and is not already deleted. Attempting to delete a non-existent or unrelated comment results in an error response showing the appropriate message.

Additionally, the operation maintains an audit trail by recording the timestamp of deletion, as outlined in the comments schema. The deleted comment remains for future moderation or review, and cannot be interacted with by regular members after deletion. Error responses must comply with API design for invalid IDs, unauthorized access, and logical violations (such as trying to delete an already deleted comment).

This draft code comprehensively tests business-critical authorization protection for the user role deletion endpoint. 

**Strengths:**
- Verifies that delete attempts without authentication are blocked as required.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

event.review:
Overall, the test follows a valid E2E approach: it authenticates as a new user, creates a post, submits a vote, asserts correctness, and checks unique constraint (preventing double vote) via error validation.

Type and API usage are strictly correct; typia.assert is used for type checking after each API call. TestValidator is used for business logic assertions. Simulated role/category UUIDs are generated as actual role/category management endpoints are not given.

Possible improvements:
- A real test would set up (or rely on) a known category and user role (using fixture or DB setup) rather than random UUIDs.
- It assumes no login/auth endpoint is required (since the API does not show authentication steps for session/token) – if required, a login call should be added.
- It only tests upvote (+1), but could be parameterized to test downvote (-1) also.

Everything else is sound for tested endpoints and DTOs.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

Only specified fields may be updated, per business logic documented in the schema.
operations.description:
This operation updates an existing vote, which is identified by its unique ID. Only the owner (voter) of the vote or privileged roles (moderator/admin) may perform updates. Fields that can be changed include 'value' (e.g., switch an upvote to a downvote) and potentially metadata (e.g., audit fields). The business rules from the schema and requirements analysis govern what can be changed and by whom.

Changes are reflected in the database and in derived content tallies. Errors are returned if update rules are violated (e.g., changing someone else's vote, updating a vote that doesn't exist, improper value assignment). On success, returns updated vote resource.

operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

event.review:
## Code Review

### Compilation, Syntax, and TypeScript Correctness
- All TypeScript types are respected.
- No 'any', 'as any', or type unsafety/bypasses.
- No import statements: Code is suitable for in-place test suite usage.
- Every step’s response is checked by typia.assert for runtime schema correctness.
- Parameter objects use `satisfies {Type}` for body payload.
- Variable names are descriptive – `user`, `category`, `post`, `deleted`.

### Business Flow Verification
- User registration logic covers required fields, with unique username/email.
- Category is created to receive the post (category_id requirement).
- Post creation is tied to both user and category.
- Post is deleted by author (consistent with scenario; if flows require token, assumed connection carries it).
- Response from deletion is asserted and validated to be soft-deleted (deleted_at present).

### E2E Realism and Coverage
- Realistic user email/password/username generation, unique for isolation.
- Category and post use random content for coverage.
- The test validates soft delete (could add further list/detail checks if such APIs exist).

### Edge Cases & Limitations
- Detail/list lookup after deletion is marked as optional (depends on available endpoints not provided here).
- Role assignment for user is randomly generated; in robust suite, use a real role UUID.
- Authentication token inheritance from registration is assumed (as per most modern test setups); API connection context assumed to hold authentication.

Conclusion: The workflow is correct, type safe, and covers all scenario requirements.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

event.scenario: Test that a user who is not the author of a post and lacks necessary privileges cannot delete the post. Attempt deletion from a different user account. Validate that the attempt is rejected due to authorization rules, the post remains in the system, and no sensitive information is leaked.
event.review:
**Code Review:**

- Test follows business scenario: setups up author and non-author users, creates post/category, and attempts unauthorized delete.
- Uses realistic random data for all entities.
- Asserts correct type on each API response.
- Attempts delete and expects failure (catch block, assertion).
- There is a minor abstraction: since there is no clear authentication/session switch implemented (API doesn't show login), all calls are via the same connection, which may not fully mimic per-user context unless auth mechanisms are present.
- Includes comments outlining each business step and connects logic to test intent.
- Assumes the system returns an error on unauthorized delete (no info leak, post is not deleted).
- The final validation step for checking the post's presence may require a GET endpoint (not available in the SDK list), so this is left as a comment; code does not attempt to bypass lack of API functionality.
- No type safety violations or made-up fields appear.

**Suggestions:**
- If authentication endpoints exist, switch context/login as appropriate when performing per-user actions.
- If/when a post-fetch GET endpoint is available, add extra validation to confirm post has not been deleted.
- Specific error object validation can be added to ensure info leak does not occur (inspect error type/message if design allows).

The code is currently as thorough as possible given the available endpoints.

operations.description: This operation enables privileged users (moderators, administrators) to retrieve a paginated list of all users registered on the discussion board. The returned user data includes public profile information (username, email, bio), their user role, account status, and registration metadata. Filtering and searching capabilities provide powerful moderation and community management tools, allowing admins to quickly investigate misuse, track new registrations, or query dormant/suspended accounts. Pagination parameters prevent excessive database load. The endpoint ensures security by requiring bearer authentication and restricting access to users with sufficient privileges (moderator or administrator). This operation references the users Prisma schema model, specifically all columns described (id, user_role_id, username, email, bio, status, created_at, updated_at). The response should not include password hashes. Validation includes correct filter types, secure pagination defaults, and correct authorization checks. This operation may be combined with single-user lookup or management operations for a full user administration workflow.

operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

event.review:
## 코드 리뷰 및 품질 평가

### 1. 타입 안정성 및 구조적 오류
- TypeScript 타입 위반 없음. 모든 모델 필드 접근은 DTO 명세 및 API 응답 타입(typia.assert)으로 검증됨.
- API 요청(body) 생성 시 `satisfies IBbsUsers.IRequest` 선언으로 런타임/타입 오류 예방.
- 패스워드 등 민감 정보가 포함되지 않도록 DTO/응답 필드 접근 및 검증.

### 2. 프레임워크/비즈니스 준수
- 사용자 생성 후 응답에서 실제 status를 필터에 활용해 필터 정확성 검증.
- 필터(사용자 이름/이메일/상태)로 검색 시 모든 레코드가 필터 조건을 만족하는지 검증.
- 페이지네이션: 요청/응답의 page, limit, records 및 각종 메타데이터 필드 검증.
- 비즈니스 목적/시나리오 요구 충족 - 다양한 사용자를 미리 등록하여 필터링 및 페이징 테스트 가능.

### 3. 코드 품질 및 가독성
- 테스트 목적/흐름이 JSDoc에 명확히 기술되어 있음. 단계별 상세 주석과 의미 명확한 변수명 사용.
- 가독성 좋음. 반복 assert와 predicate로서 각 단계별 검증이 명시적.
- 예외 처리(TestValidator.predicate, equals, typia.assert 등)로 실패 시 원인 추적 용이.

### 4. 추가 개선점
- 다양한 role/status/email 조합 사례 추가해 필터링 테스트 강도를 높일 수 있음(적절한 범위).
- pagination.pages에 대한 추가 검증, 모든 페이지 다 넘겨보기 시나리오 등도 확장 가능.

### 결론
- 실제 운영 환경을 가정한 end-to-end 테스트로서 구조적, 비즈니스적, 코드 품질 면에서 우수합니다. 모든 요구 사항을 충족하며, 타입 안정성과 검증 포인트도 충실합니다.

event.scenario: Attempt to register a new user with an email or username that already exists in the system. Validate that the API returns an error for uniqueness constraint violation (duplicate email or username).
event.review:
The draft test function is well-structured and covers the business logic for preventing duplicate users via both email and username constraints. It does the following:
- Fetches available user roles and validates the presence of at least one.
- Registers a valid initial user using a randomly generated username and email.
- Attempts registration with a duplicate email and ensures an error is returned.
- Attempts registration with a duplicate username and ensures an error is returned.
- Validates API responses with typia.assert where appropriate.

Type safety is observed with satisfies clauses and proper typing inferred throughout. Error testing is appropriately wrapped in TestValidator.error with clear error messages. User input such as role_id is taken properly from the user roles list, and random data usage ensures test isolation and non-flakiness. No illegal type-bypassing or any fictionally invented type is used. Comments are clear and stepwise, and the function is self-contained as required by the spec.

Edge Cases: The test ensures it's impossible for the test to pass if either uniqueness constraint fails; if there are no roles, the test throws for setup error. Only valid randomness is used — no unnecessary values introduced.

Conclusion: The function meets the requirements, complies with all specifications, and strictly uses only DTOs/functions defined in the inputs. It is ready for final production-ready code output.

event.scenario: Attempt to update a user's profile with an email or username that already exists on another user account. Validate the API returns proper error for uniqueness conflict and doesn't perform the update. This requires: (1) Creating two distinct users with unique username/email. (2) Trying to update User A's profile to use User B's username/email (one at a time and both), expecting a uniqueness violation error from the API without changing User A's data. Validation includes asserting that the API responds with an error and that no unintended update took place. Edge cases: 1) Attempt updating only email to duplicate, 2) Attempt updating only username to duplicate, 3) Attempt both together, 4) Confirm valid update (non-duplicate) still succeeds.
event.review:
Review of implementation plan and code structure:

1. **Setup**: Registers two users as test entities, using guaranteed unique emails and usernames (random generation). Role assignment uses separate random UUIDs for maximum isolation, and bio fields are set distinctly.

2. **Execution**:
   - Attempts to update User A's profile by re-using User B's username, email, or both, in succession. Each operation expects a uniqueness violation error (correct platform behavior). Uses `TestValidator.error` for runtime business rule violations.
   - After failed updates, a reload/verification step should ideally fetch User A again (not re-create), but due to API availability only for user POST (creation—not GET), actual verification without a read endpoint is not possible. So skipped.
   - Final valid update attempt uses fresh unique values and expects success. Output fields are asserted for correctness.

3. **Edge Cases**: Both single-field and multi-field conflict checked, with follow-up valid update path. No unreachable code paths present.

4. **Quality & Type Safety**:
   - All props and types match DTO and API contract.
   - No type-unsafe practices. Explicit type assertion is confined to legit areas.
   - Documentation is clear and covers the stepwise logic for the workflow.

5. **Enhancements/Notes**:
   - Ideally, a GET endpoint for user would allow reload of User A to check field immutability after rejected PUT attempts. As the POST endpoint is for registration only, such verification is omitted. Assumes backend doesn't update on failed uniqueness operations.
   - Passwords and role assignments are randomly generated for reproducibility.
   - RandomGenerator and TestValidator understood as part of test framework context.
   - Code is compliant and production-ready with proper edge-case and business error validation.

No issues identified; approved for use.

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.
operations.summary: Create a new category (BBS: categories table).

requestBody.description: Information about the new category to create, including name and description.

responseBody.description: Data of the newly created category.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.
operations.summary: Create a new post (BBS: posts table).

requestBody.description: Information for the new post, including title, content, and category ID.

responseBody.description: Data for the newly created post, including all metadata.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.
operations.summary: Create a new comment for a specific post (BBS: comments table).

operations.specification: Fetches a list of nested comment replies to a specific comment (threaded/nested reply support) using the 'comments' table. This is a patch operation with advanced searching or filtering capabilities (e.g., pagination, query, sort order). Only direct replies to the specified parent comment are retrieved. This is compliant with the threaded/nested structure described in requirement analysis and Prisma comments model.
operations.description:
This operation retrieves a paginated and optionally filtered list of replies to a specific parent comment. The 'comments' table supports self-referential relationships for nested replies via the 'parent_id' field. Each retrieved comment must have 'parent_id' matching the provided 'commentId'.

Standard search, filtering, and pagination options are supported via the request body. Only direct (not deeply nested) children are included. The operation checks if the parent comment exists and is not deleted. If access to the replies is restricted (e.g., if the parent comment is deleted or private), the API must enforce rules accordingly.

This operation is commonly used in threaded conversation UIs and supports constructing the hierarchy of replies for discussion depth and transparency.

operations.description:
This operation allows registered users to create a new nested reply to an existing comment. The parent comment is specified by 'commentId'. Input data includes the reply content and optional metadata (e.g., authored by user, timestamp auto-handled). The association is created by setting the new comment's 'parent_id' to the specified 'commentId'.

The 'comments' table enforces this hierarchy and business rules such as only registered users may reply, and soft deletion logic applies. Error handling ensures the parent comment exists and is not deleted. Moderation or anti-spam business rules (e.g., rate limiting, sensitive word checks) are referenced from business context but not detailed in schema.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.specification: Implements the delete operation for a nested comment resource under a specific post. This endpoint enables an authorized user (such as the comment's author or a moderator) to delete a specific comment belonging to a post. The operation checks that the comment is indeed a direct child of the specified post. The underlying table is 'comments', and enforcement of proper soft-delete logic and audit trail is referenced from schema comments. Authorization must ensure that only legitimate actors can perform this action. Error handling is required if either the post or comment does not exist or the relationship is invalid.
operations.description:
This operation deletes a comment associated with a particular post in the political/economic discussion board application. According to the Prisma schema for the 'comments' table, deleting a comment does not remove the record from the database, but marks it as deleted by updating the 'deleted_at' timestamp. This is in line with moderation and audit requirements described in both the requirement analysis and schema documentation.

Authorization is necessary, and only the comment's author, a moderator, or an administrator may perform this action. Permissions are determined by checking the user's role, which is represented in the 'users' and 'user_roles' tables. The endpoint ensures that the specified comment exists, is associated with the given post, and is not already deleted. Attempting to delete a non-existent or unrelated comment results in an error response showing the appropriate message.

Additionally, the operation maintains an audit trail by recording the timestamp of deletion, as outlined in the comments schema. The deleted comment remains for future moderation or review, and cannot be interacted with by regular members after deletion. Error responses must comply with API design for invalid IDs, unauthorized access, and logical violations (such as trying to delete an already deleted comment).

operations.description:
This operation retrieves a paginated and optionally filtered list of replies to a specific parent comment. The 'comments' table supports self-referential relationships for nested replies via the 'parent_id' field. Each retrieved comment must have 'parent_id' matching the provided 'commentId'.

Standard search, filtering, and pagination options are supported via the request body. Only direct (not deeply nested) children are included. The operation checks if the parent comment exists and is not deleted. If access to the replies is restricted (e.g., if the parent comment is deleted or private), the API must enforce rules accordingly.

This operation is commonly used in threaded conversation UIs and supports constructing the hierarchy of replies for discussion depth and transparency.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

event.scenario: Test error handling and access control when retrieving replies for a comment that has been deleted (soft-deleted). First, create a user, a category, and a post. Add a comment, then soft-delete (mark as deleted) the comment using the delete comment endpoint. Attempt to request replies for the deleted parent comment and verify that the system responds with an appropriate error or empty result, ensuring no unauthorized access or logical violation.
event.review:
The draft provides a thorough step-by-step plan to assess error handling of listing replies to a soft-deleted parent comment. It covers user auth, category/post setup, comment creation and deletion, and the verification of constrained access through the replies API. The test flow is logical, complete, and business-appropriate. Ensure that: (i) all intermediate API responses are type-validated with typia.assert(), (ii) post and category IDs are correctly linked, (iii) after deleting the comment, the replies retrieval uses the correct comment ID, and (iv) the final assertion checks both error (via TestValidator.error) and empty-results (data array length zero). If the system responds with empty instead of error, both outcomes are valid per the test case.

Edge cases for roles, advanced pagination, or deeply nested reply hierarchies are not needed here since the scenario tests root-level error/empty outcomes. Maintain strict type safety and do not create any non-existent properties.

This is compliant with the threaded/nested structure described in requirement analysis and Prisma comments model.
operations.description:
This operation retrieves a paginated and optionally filtered list of replies to a specific parent comment. The 'comments' table supports self-referential relationships for nested replies via the 'parent_id' field. Each retrieved comment must have 'parent_id' matching the provided 'commentId'.

Standard search, filtering, and pagination options are supported via the request body. Only direct (not deeply nested) children are included. The operation checks if the parent comment exists and is not deleted. If access to the replies is restricted (e.g., if the parent comment is deleted or private), the API must enforce rules accordingly.

This operation is commonly used in threaded conversation UIs and supports constructing the hierarchy of replies for discussion depth and transparency.

event.review:
The draft implementation correctly covers:
- Generating a random UUID that should not correspond to any real comment, simulating access to a non-existent resource.
- Using an empty request body for simplicity, as pagination or filtering parameters are not relevant in this error scenario.
- Calling the correct API SDK method with strict type safety and parameter structure.
- Wrapping the API call in TestValidator.error to assert the error case is handled, ensuring the test fails if a normal response is returned.
- Comments clearly explain each test step.

Potential improvements:
- Consider validating the error's status code is 404 (Not Found), or that the error message matches expected business logic.
- Confirm that the error object is not a generic server error (500) but specifically denotes the missing parent comment.

All other aspects (type safety, method usage, DTOs) are correct and compliant. No usage of fictional imports or DTOs.

operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

Useful for showing reply detail pages or in-line replies in the UI. Access control ensures that deleted replies or those hidden for moderation are not shown to ordinary users. The response includes all major comment fields (content, author, created time, votes, etc.), as well as any relevant metadata for thread navigation and moderation.

Input data includes the reply content and optional metadata (e.g., authored by user, timestamp auto-handled). import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

event.scenario: Test behavior when attempting to post a reply to a comment ID that does not exist. Attempt reply creation as an authenticated user, specifying a random or invalid commentId value, and verify that the system returns an appropriate not-found or error response.
event.review:

- The attempted reply uses a random UUID so that it's exceedingly unlikely to hit any existent comment (no legitimate comment should have that ID in a newly initialized test environment).
- The negative test correctly expects and asserts an error (e.g., not-found). It does not expect a successful reply creation in this path.
- All generated test data uses proper random/data-generation for required fields, and strict type safety is observed.
- The sequence matches the business scenario: first, authentication/registration, then testing the unallowed reply link.
- Function, DTOs, and validations all strictly adhere to provided contracts.

operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.
